===== REQUIREMENTS (stage-1.md, verbatim) =====

# Tablekeeper — Stage 1: reservations

This stage defines the initial service and its API.

Build from the supplied requirements. Source code, API documentation and schemas from
existing products in this domain must not be used.

## 1. Scope

Diners can search restaurant availability, book a table and receive a confirmation
reference. They can cancel or amend their bookings, including changing several bookings
together. Each restaurant has its own table capacities, opening hours and cancellation policy.
Only the HTTP API is required.

Two `confirmed` reservations must never occupy the same table at overlapping times,
including during concurrent requests. Occupancy is the half-open interval
`[starts_at, starts_at + reservation_duration)`. A 90-minute booking at 19:00 therefore
does not overlap a booking starting at 20:30. Retries and rejected requests must not
create duplicate or partial bookings.

## 2. Delivery and deployment

Deliver an HTTP service, a `Dockerfile` and a `RUN.md` with a command that builds and
starts the service without manual setup. Language, framework and storage are unrestricted.
A `docker-compose.yml` is optional.

The submission is a containerized HTTP service, not a Python package. Python is not
required in the implementation. TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, Python and any
other language are equally valid. The harness builds the submitted `Dockerfile`, starts
the resulting image and tests only its HTTP behavior; it does not import or execute the
submission's source files on the judge host.

The image must run on its own with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping. Runtime networking
has no outbound access. All runtime dependencies, initialization and seed data must work
within that single container. Compose configuration is not used to start the service.

### Resource limits

The service must operate within these limits:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2 vCPU |
| Memory | 2 GiB |
| Start to first healthy response | 60 s |
| Concurrent requests | up to 50 in flight |
| Per-request timeout | 5 s (10 s for `POST /_test/reset`) |
| Outbound network | available during `docker build`, **none at run time** |
| Disk | ephemeral; state need not survive a container restart |

Runtime assets and dependencies must be included in the image. This includes fonts,
scripts and stylesheets; external services are unavailable at runtime.

## 3. Runtime contract

### 3.1 Listening

Listen on `0.0.0.0` using the `PORT` environment variable, default `8080`.

### 3.2 Health

```http
GET /health  ->  200  {"status": "ok"}
```

Return 200 once the service and its data store can serve requests, within 60 seconds
of container start. Non-200 responses are permitted before the service is ready.

### 3.3 Reset and seed

```http
POST /_test/reset
Content-Type: application/json

{ ...fixture... }

->  204 No Content
```

Replace all service state with the fixture in the request body (§4). When reset returns
204, subsequent requests must see only that fixture. Repeated resets are supported.
This test endpoint must be enabled in the delivered image and requires no authentication.

### 3.4 Conventions

- Requests and responses are `application/json; charset=utf-8`.
- Timestamps in responses are RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, e.g. `2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00`.
- Unknown fields in a request body are ignored, never an error.
- Unknown query parameters are ignored.
- IDs are opaque strings of at most 64 characters. Their format is yours. This limit
  also applies to IDs supplied in reset fixtures.

## 4. Model

Restaurants and tables are supplied through `POST /_test/reset` only. Restaurant and
table creation endpoints are out of scope.

| Field | On | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `timezone` | Restaurant | IANA zone name, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. All of the restaurant's times are local to this |
| `slot_minutes` | Restaurant | Bookings start on a grid of this many minutes from opening time |
| `reservation_duration_minutes` | Restaurant | How long every reservation occupies its table |
| `cancellation_cutoff_minutes` | Restaurant | A booking cannot be cancelled or changed within this many minutes of its start |
| `opening_hours` | Restaurant | Per weekday. A day with no entry is closed |
| `capacity` | Table | Maximum party size |

### Fixture format

```json
{
  "users": [
    { "id": "u_ada", "email": "ada@example.com",
      "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada" }
  ],
  "restaurants": [
    {
      "id": "r_anker",
      "name": "Zum Anker",
      "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
      "slot_minutes": 30,
      "reservation_duration_minutes": 90,
      "cancellation_cutoff_minutes": 120,
      "opening_hours": [
        { "weekday": "thu", "opens": "18:00", "closes": "23:00" },
        { "weekday": "fri", "opens": "18:00", "closes": "23:30" }
      ],
      "tables": [
        { "id": "t_1", "label": "1", "capacity": 2 },
        { "id": "t_2", "label": "2", "capacity": 4 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "reservations": []
}
```

- `weekday` is one of `mon tue wed thu fri sat sun`.
- `opens` and `closes` are local `HH:MM`, 24-hour. `closes` is always later than `opens` on the
  same local day — opening hours never cross midnight.
- Seeded users must be able to log in with the given password immediately.
- `reservations` may seed confirmed bookings, with the same fields as a `POST /reservations`
  body plus `id`, `reference` and `user_id`.

Fixtures may use any calendar date. A booking must not be rejected solely because its
start is in the past; the cancellation and amendment cutoff rules still apply.

## 5. Errors

Every 4xx and 5xx response carries this body:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "table_unavailable", "message": "human readable, any wording" } }
```

Use the specified HTTP status and `code`. The human-readable `message` may use any wording.
Endpoint-specific errors are listed with each endpoint.

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `malformed_request` | Unparseable body, or a field of the wrong JSON type |
| 400 | `missing_idempotency_key` | Required `Idempotency-Key` header absent or empty |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token |
| 403 | `forbidden` | Authenticated, but not permitted to touch this resource |
| 404 | `not_found` | No such resource, or not visible to this caller |
| 409 | `idempotency_key_reuse` | Key already used by this caller with a different request body |
| 422 | `validation_failed` | A required field or query parameter is missing, or a stated rule is violated with no more specific code |

A field of the correct JSON type with an invalid format or out-of-range value gives
422 `validation_failed`, unless an endpoint specifies a different error. This includes
invalid dates, negative counts and values exceeding a stated maximum or length. In addition:

- Endpoint-specific field rules take precedence: invalid `party_size` values (including strings
  and booleans) and `starts_at_local` strings that are not a bare local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` are
  422 `validation_failed`. Other wrong JSON types follow the rule below.
- An integer-valued **query parameter** is written as plain decimal digits: `1e9`, `4.0` and `+4`
  are 422 `validation_failed` whatever their numeric value.
- Reserve 400 `malformed_request` for a body that does not parse or a field of the wrong type.

Shared ranges, enforced on every endpoint that takes them:

| Field | Valid | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | 1 to 255 characters | 422 `validation_failed` |

Requests must not produce 5xx responses, including under concurrent load.

## 6. Authentication

Authentication supports signup and login. Email verification, password reset, refresh
tokens and role-management endpoints are out of scope. Permissions specified elsewhere
in these requirements still apply.

```http
POST /auth/signup
{ "email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada" }

->  201  { "user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..." }
```

```http
POST /auth/login
{ "email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse" }

->  200  { "user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..." }
```

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Email already registered | 409 `email_taken` |
| Password shorter than 8 characters | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `email` not of the form `local@domain` | 422 `validation_failed` |
| Wrong password or unknown email on login | 401 `unauthenticated` |

Every other endpoint requires a bearer token, except `/health`, `/_test/reset`, the two above, and
the three public endpoints named at the top of §8 — `GET /restaurants`, `GET /restaurants/{id}` and
`GET /availability`:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Tokens do not expire. An account may have multiple valid tokens and concurrent sessions.

Passwords must be stored using a password-hashing function such as bcrypt, scrypt or
Argon2, or an equivalent. Plaintext password storage is not permitted.

## 7. Idempotency

Two write paths require an idempotency key: **`POST /reservations`** (§8) and
**`POST /reservation-moves`** (§11).

```http
Idempotency-Key: <client-chosen string, 1..255 characters>
```

The key is scoped to **the authenticated user**. Two different users may use the same key string
with no interaction between them.

A replay means the same user sending the **same method, the same path and the same body**. The
same key with the same body on a different path is a different request, not a replay, and must
succeed normally.

After the body has been parsed as a JSON object and the caller authenticated, idempotency
is resolved before endpoint-specific field validation or current-resource checks. Thus a
used key with a different JSON body returns `409 idempotency_key_reuse` even when that new
body would otherwise be invalid.

| Situation | Response |
|---|---|
| Header absent or empty | 400 `missing_idempotency_key` |
| First use of the key | The normal response, **201** |
| Replay: same key, same body | **200**, body identical to the original response as a JSON value |
| Same key, different body | 409 `idempotency_key_reuse` |
| Key reused after the original request failed with 4xx | Treated as a first use |

"Same body" means the same JSON value after parsing — key order and whitespace do not matter.

For concurrent identical requests with an unused key, exactly one returns 201.
The others return 200 with the same body. The operation takes effect only once.

A successful replay returns the original response, even after the resource changes or
is cancelled. It makes no further state changes.

## 8. API

`GET /restaurants`, `GET /restaurants/{id}` and `GET /availability` are **public** — no bearer
token. Everything else needs one. Diners browse before they sign in.

### `GET /restaurants`

```json
{ "restaurants": [ { "id": "r_anker", "name": "Zum Anker", "timezone": "Europe/Berlin" } ] }
```

### `GET /restaurants/{id}`

The restaurant with its `slot_minutes`, `reservation_duration_minutes`,
`cancellation_cutoff_minutes`, `opening_hours` and `tables`, in the fixture's shape. 404 if
unknown.

### `GET /availability`

```http
GET /availability?restaurant_id=r_anker&date=2026-09-24&party_size=4
```

All three parameters are required; a missing one is 422 `validation_failed`. `date` is a local
calendar date at the restaurant.

```json
{
  "restaurant_id": "r_anker",
  "date": "2026-09-24",
  "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
  "slots": [
    { "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T18:00",
      "starts_at": "2026-09-24T18:00:00+02:00",
      "available_table_ids": ["t_2"] }
  ]
}
```

`starts_at_local` is the full `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` and goes into `POST /reservations` unchanged.

A slot appears for every `slot_minutes` step from `opens` such that
`slot + reservation_duration_minutes <= closes`. `available_table_ids` lists the tables of that
restaurant with `capacity >= party_size` and no overlapping confirmed reservation, in fixture
order. A slot with no available table still appears, with an empty list.

A closed day returns `"slots": []`.

### `POST /reservations`

`Idempotency-Key` is required; see §7.

```http
POST /reservations
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: 2f9c1a...

{ "restaurant_id": "r_anker", "table_id": "t_2",
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00", "party_size": 4 }
```

`starts_at_local` is wall-clock at the restaurant, with no offset and no `Z`. Resolve it against
the restaurant's `timezone`.

```json
201
{
  "reservation_id": "res_7",
  "reference": "K3P7QW",
  "restaurant_id": "r_anker",
  "table_id": "t_2",
  "party_size": 4,
  "status": "confirmed",
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00",
  "starts_at": "2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00",
  "ends_at": "2026-09-24T20:30:00+02:00",
  "created_at": "2026-09-21T11:04:03+00:00"
}
```

`reference` is 6 to 12 characters of `A-Z0-9`, unique across all reservations, and never changes.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| The table is taken for an overlapping interval | 409 `table_unavailable` |
| `starts_at_local` is not on the slot grid | 422 `not_on_slot_grid` |
| Slot outside opening hours, or the reservation would end after `closes` | 422 `outside_opening_hours` |
| `party_size` exceeds the table's `capacity` | 422 `party_exceeds_capacity` |
| `party_size` below 1, or not an integer | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `starts_at_local` is a local time that does not exist (see §9) | 422 `invalid_local_time` |
| Unknown restaurant, unknown table, or the table belongs to another restaurant | 404 `not_found` |

### `GET /reservations`

The caller's reservations, `starts_at` descending, confirmed and cancelled alike.
Return `200` with `{"reservations": [...]}`; each entry has the same shape as the
create response. An empty list is `{"reservations": []}`.

### `GET /reservations/{reference}`

One reservation. **404 if it is not the caller's** — do not leak the existence of other people's
bookings.

### `POST /reservations/{reference}/cancel`

```json
200
{ "reference": "K3P7QW", "status": "cancelled", ... }
```

Frees the table immediately: the next `GET /availability` must offer that slot again.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Already cancelled | 200 with the current state — cancelling twice is not an error |
| Now is within `cancellation_cutoff_minutes` of `starts_at`, or later | 409 `cutoff_passed` |
| Not the caller's reservation | 404 `not_found` |

### `PATCH /reservations/{reference}`

Change the time, the table or the party size. Any subset of `table_id`, `starts_at_local`,
`party_size`. No idempotency key is required here.

Validation is identical to `POST /reservations`, and the same cutoff rule as cancel applies
(409 `cutoff_passed`), measured against the **current** start time. A cancelled reservation is
409 `reservation_cancelled`. A successful amendment releases the old slot and reserves the
new one together. A failed amendment leaves the original booking and its occupancy unchanged.

`reference` and `reservation_id` survive a change.

## 9. Time and DST

Local dates and times follow the restaurant's `timezone`, including daylight-saving transitions.

**Spring forward.** Local times in the skipped hour do not exist. They never appear in
availability, and booking one is 422 `invalid_local_time`.

**Fall back.** Local times in the repeated hour occur twice. **Always resolve to the first
occurrence — the one before the clocks change.** The slot appears once in availability, and the
second occurrence is not bookable.

`reservation_duration_minutes` is **absolute time**, not wall-clock. A 90-minute reservation
starting at 01:30 on a fall-back night ends 90 real minutes later, and its local `ends_at` will
read 02:00, not 03:00.

The transitions that must be handled:

| Zone | Spring forward | Fall back |
|---|---|---|
| `Europe/Berlin` | 2026-03-29, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-10-25, 03:00 → 02:00 |
| `America/New_York` | 2026-03-08, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-11-01, 02:00 → 01:00 |

Offsets must follow the IANA rules for the specified zone and date.

## 10. Export and import

The service must support `GET /_test/export` and `POST /_test/import`. Like reset, these
are unauthenticated test endpoints.
Exports may contain credentials and session tokens; handle them as private test artifacts.
Return 200 from export with a JSON object containing `track: "tablekeeper"`,
`format_version: 1` and `state` (an implementation-defined JSON object). The state format
is opaque to the caller and must be accepted unchanged by import.

Import takes that entire object and atomically replaces the service's state, returning
204. It must accept an unchanged export produced by this service. No dependency on the
source process, files, volume, port or network address is allowed. Import is replacement,
not merge; repeating it restores the exported state without duplicating anything. Invalid
JSON follows §5; missing fields, wrong track/version or an invalid state give 422
`validation_failed` without changing the destination. Test control calls have a 10-second
timeout. Export is an atomic, read-only snapshot; subsequent source writes do not change it.

Preserve accounts and hashed-password login, existing bearer tokens, fixture configuration,
reservations, references, all completed idempotent request bodies and original responses.
Identities, statuses and timestamps must not be regenerated. Failed request keys remain
reusable. Existing receipts, references, tokens and retries must remain valid after import;
replacing the state with a fresh fixture does not satisfy this requirement. Import removes
all previous destination data and credentials. Reset continues to clear all state, including
imported state. State need not survive an abrupt container restart.

## 11. Atomic reservation moves

A diner may change several bookings in one request.

`POST /reservation-moves` requires authentication and an idempotency key. Body:

```json
{"moves": [{"reference": "BOOK01", "table_id": "t_2"},
           {"reference": "BOOK02", "table_id": "t_1"}]}
```

`moves` contains 1..8 objects with distinct string references. Invalid shape or duplicate
references gives 422 `validation_failed`. Every booking must belong to the caller and the
same restaurant. Unknown/another owner's reference gives 404 `not_found`; different
restaurants give 422 `validation_failed`. No token gives 401.

Each item accepts the ordinary PATCH fields `table_id`, `starts_at_local`, `party_size`;
omitted fields retain their current values and unknown fields are ignored. The booking's
identity, owner and creation time never change. Cancelled bookings give 409
`reservation_cancelled`. Each booking's existing cutoff applies. Non-occupancy errors use
ordinary amendment codes and take precedence in input order, with cutoff errors preceding
other changes for that booking. An overlap among resulting bookings or with an unlisted
booking gives 409 `table_unavailable`. Unchanged listed bookings retain their occupancy.

Either every move commits or nothing changes: occupancy, reservation records and retry
keys. On success return 201 with `{"reservations": [...]}` in input order, including
unchanged items.
Replays return that original response with 200, even after amendments or cancellations.
No-op moves retain all existing values. Export/import preserves successful batch receipts
as well as the resulting bookings. No batch UI is required.

## Acknowledge before you start

The moment you receive a handoff, and before you read anything or write a line, reply to
the seat that sent it with a short acknowledgement: that you have it, and the order you
intend to work in. Two or three sentences. Then begin.

This is not a courtesy. Work can be interrupted at any point by something outside the
band, and a factory whose collaboration is only visible at the end has no record of
having collaborated at all. Acknowledge first, report progress at each committed
milestone, and never leave the room with nothing in it while you work.

stage-1: service-level checks for load, retries and daylight saving

Written from the requirements rather than from the shipped sample, and aimed at
what the sample never exercises.

Load, at the stated budget of 50 requests in flight: fifty accounts racing for
one table, fifty racing for merely overlapping intervals, fifty identical
retries of one key, fifty amendments onto one free table, a cancel-and-rebook
race, fifty concurrent swap batches, and a mixed load that includes malformed
and rejected requests. Each asserts no 5xx and then re-derives the no-double-
booking invariant from the public API.

Retries: that a used key with an otherwise invalid body is a reuse rather than a
validation failure, that the same key on another path is a different request,
that a key spent on a 4xx is reusable, that key order and whitespace do not
change a body, and that a replay after a cancellation or an amendment returns
the original response and changes nothing.

Time: both transitions in both named zones -- the skipped hour absent from
availability and unbookable, the repeated hour appearing once and resolving to
its first occurrence, durations measured in absolute time either side, and the
consequence that the repeated hour offers one hour of capacity rather than two.

Three expectations were wrong and were corrected against the requirements, not
the service: adjacent intervals mean two bookings can win a five-slot race, the
end of a reservation that crosses a fall-back carries the new offset, and a
booking in the past cannot be amended because its cutoff has passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Committed so far: f2a541b (service, Dockerfile, RUN.md) and 77ad728 (my own service-level checks for load, retries, DST). Go, single container, scratch image with the IANA database compiled into the binary, deps vendored in-repo so the build needs no module fetch and the runtime needs no network. Whole store behind one mutex held for each request's entire decision, which is what makes no-double-booking hold under load without retries; bcrypt is kept outside that lock.

Evidence run so far, all against the built image (docker build -t tablekeeper stage-1; docker run -e PORT=8080 -p 18080:8080):
- supplied kickoff stage_1 checks: 120 passed in 297s (I did not edit them).
- my concurrency suite: 8 passed - 50 in flight racing one table (exactly one 201, 49 x 409), 50 racing overlapping intervals, 50 identical retries of one key (one 201, 49 x 200, one booking), 50 amendments onto one free table, cancel/rebook race, 50 concurrent swap batches, a mixed 50-request load including malformed input, health under load. No 5xx anywhere; invariant re-derived from the public API each time.
- my idempotency suite: 17 passed - including precedence (used key + invalid body = 409, not 422), same key on a different path, key reusable after 4xx, body equality modulo key order/whitespace, replay after cancel/amend returns the original and changes nothing.
- my DST suite: 27 passed - both transitions in Europe/Berlin and America/New_York, skipped hour absent and unbookable, repeated hour once and first-occurrence, absolute-time durations either side, seeded fixtures at skipped/repeated times.

Still to write and run: atomic moves, export/import fidelity (tokens, idempotency receipts, move receipts, cross-container), error codes/precedence and password hashing. Will report the final commit hash with the full output.

base="http://127.0.0.1:18080"

    clients=[httpx.Client(base_url=base, timeout=30) for _ in range(n)]
    if prewarm:
        for c in clients: c.get("/health")
    gate=threading.Barrier(n)
    def go(i):
        gate.wait(); s=time.time(); r=fn(clients[i], i); return r.status_code, time.time()-s
    t=time.time()
    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=n) as ex:
        out=[f.result() for f in [ex.submit(go,i) for i in range(n)]]

{"args":{"command":"cd "/c/Users/Hamza Bukhari/Downloads/HW 01/dark-factory/run2" && git add -A stage-1 && git -c user.email="mlearningdrive@gmail.com" -c user.name="coder" commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
stage-1: checks for moves, export/import, errors and reads; fit bcrypt to the budget

Four more suites, and one behaviour change they paid for.

The suites: atomic moves (swaps and rotations that no sequence of single
amendments could make, error precedence in input order, cutoff before a
booking's other changes, rollback of everything including the retry key, batch
receipts), export and import (bookings, tokens, hashed-password login,
idempotency and batch receipts, failed keys still reusable, replacement rather
than merge, snapshot isolation from later writes, rejected envelopes leaving the
destination untouched, and a snapshot imported into a second container on a
different port), the error table (status and code for every stated case, the
order between malformed, unauthenticated, missing-key, reuse and validation,
and fixture validation), and the reads (slot grid under several configurations,
capacity and fixture order, the booking lifecycle, cutoffs).

The change: the bcrypt work factor drops from 10 to 8. Measured on the stated
budget of 2 vCPU, the slowest of 50 concurrent logins took 6.7 s at cost 10,
which breaks the 5 s per-request limit, and seeding 50 accounts through reset
took 5.9 s of its 10 s. At cost 8 the same bursts measure 1.56 s and 1.22 s.
Passwords are still hashed with bcrypt; the factor is the highest that fits the
resource limits rather than the highest available.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@[[32488f46-a3a3-4703-8384-9151e27da41a]] Stage 1 done. Commit 126cf6bc5354edf1b00de78a83658a354ce0cbb3 (three commits: f2a541b service+Dockerfile+RUN.md, 77ad728 first three test suites, 126cf6b remaining suites + bcrypt cost fix). No amends, no rebases. Everything is under stage-1/.

WHAT IT IS
Go, no framework. Scratch image + static binary with the IANA database compiled in (time/tzdata); the only dependency (x/crypto/bcrypt) is vendored in-repo, so the build needs no module fetch and the runtime needs no network. The whole store sits behind one mutex that each request holds for its entire decision, so a booking decision and the write it implies cannot be split: that is how no-double-booking holds at 50 in flight without optimistic retries, and why a rejected batch can never leave a partial state. bcrypt is deliberately outside that lock. Occupancy is half-open intervals of absolute time. A wall-clock stamp is resolved by sampling the zone offsets either side of it and keeping only candidates that read back as the same wall clock, so a skipped hour has no instant and a repeated hour yields its first occurrence. One state type is store, export payload and import payload, with one validator gating all three, so neither a fixture nor an import can install a world the API could not have produced. Reservation timestamps are stored as rendered RFC 3339 strings so a round trip hands back the same timestamps rather than new ones.

COMMANDS RUN AND REAL RESULTS (all against the built image)
- docker build -t tablekeeper stage-1 -> ok. Also 'docker build --network=none --no-cache' -> ok, which proves the vendoring.
- docker run --rm --cpus 2 --memory 2g -e PORT=8080 -p 8080:8080 tablekeeper; GET /health -> 200 {"status":"ok"} in under a second (budget 60 s). A second container on PORT=9000 also serves.
- Supplied kickoff checks, unedited: python -m pytest tablekeeper/test/stage_1 -p harness.plugin --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18080 -q -> 120 passed in 182.73s.
- My own suite: python -m pytest stage-1/tests -q --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18080 --second-base-url http://127.0.0.1:19090 -> 292 passed in 32.47s. Breakdown: concurrency 8, idempotency 17, DST 27, moves 32, export/import 28, errors+auth 145, availability+bookings 35.
- No-outbound-network proof: service on a docker --internal network, reached by container name from a sibling container -> /health 200, reset 204, availability at the Berlin fall-back returned correct +02:00/+01:00 offsets; the same network could not reach proxy.golang.org (curl exit 28).
- gofmt -l clean, go vet clean.

ONE REAL DEFECT I FOUND AND FIXED
At the bcrypt library default (cost 10), measured on the stated 2 vCPU budget: the slowest of 50 concurrent logins took 6.7 s, breaking the 5 s per-request limit, and seeding 50 accounts via reset took 5.9 s of its 10 s. At cost 8 the same bursts measure 1.56 s and 1.22 s. Passwords are still bcrypt; the factor is the highest that fits the resource limits, and the reasoning is in a comment at the constant.

ASSUMPTIONS WHERE THE REQUIREMENTS ARE SILENT (each one is testable, so please have @verifier challenge them)
1. Unknown body fields are ignored when acting on a request, but they are part of the body for idempotency: a retry that adds a field is 409 idempotency_key_reuse, not a 200 replay. Section 7 says 'the same JSON value after parsing'.
2. party_size in a body must be a plain integer token: 4.0 is 422, matching section 5's explicit rule for integer query parameters.
3. display_name is required on signup (422 if absent).
4. Field format validation precedes resource lookup at the top of a request (so a bad Idempotency-Key length is 422 before any 404), but inside booking resolution the order is section 8's table: unknown restaurant/table 404, then invalid_local_time, then not_on_slot_grid, then outside_opening_hours, then party_exceeds_capacity, then table_unavailable. A closed day answers outside_opening_hours rather than not_on_slot_grid, since a closed day has no grid.
5. In a batch, a booking's cancelled check and its cutoff are decided before anything it was asked to change, and errors otherwise follow input order.
6. An amendment does not re-validate a field it was not asked to change, so a party-size change never trips the slot grid.
7. A reset fixture or an import is rejected 422 when it is internally inconsistent: duplicate ids or emails, unknown timezone, closes <= opens, duplicate weekday, capacity < 1, references outside A-Z0-9{6,12}, unknown user/restaurant/table, a seeded start in a skipped local hour, or two confirmed bookings overlapping on one table.
8. An id longer than 64 characters is 422 rather than 404, per section 5's length rule.
9. A method the service does not offer on a known path answers 404 not_found with the error envelope; section 5 names no code for it.

NOT DONE: nothing in stage 1 that I am aware of. I did not touch the supplied checks and wrote nothing aimed at them; three of my own expectations were wrong and I corrected them against the requirements (adjacent intervals let two bookings win a five-slot race; the end of a booking crossing a fall-back carries the new offset; a past booking cannot be amended because its cutoff has passed). Stopping here as instructed.

===== REQUIREMENTS (stage-1.md, verbatim) =====

# Tablekeeper — Stage 1: reservations

This stage defines the initial service and its API.

Build from the supplied requirements. Source code, API documentation and schemas from
existing products in this domain must not be used.

## 1. Scope

Diners can search restaurant availability, book a table and receive a confirmation
reference. They can cancel or amend their bookings, including changing several bookings
together. Each restaurant has its own table capacities, opening hours and cancellation policy.
Only the HTTP API is required.

Two `confirmed` reservations must never occupy the same table at overlapping times,
including during concurrent requests. Occupancy is the half-open interval
`[starts_at, starts_at + reservation_duration)`. A 90-minute booking at 19:00 therefore
does not overlap a booking starting at 20:30. Retries and rejected requests must not
create duplicate or partial bookings.

## 2. Delivery and deployment

Deliver an HTTP service, a `Dockerfile` and a `RUN.md` with a command that builds and
starts the service without manual setup. Language, framework and storage are unrestricted.
A `docker-compose.yml` is optional.

The submission is a containerized HTTP service, not a Python package. Python is not
required in the implementation. TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, Python and any
other language are equally valid. The harness builds the submitted `Dockerfile`, starts
the resulting image and tests only its HTTP behavior; it does not import or execute the
submission's source files on the judge host.

The image must run on its own with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping. Runtime networking
has no outbound access. All runtime dependencies, initialization and seed data must work
within that single container. Compose configuration is not used to start the service.

### Resource limits

The service must operate within these limits:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2 vCPU |
| Memory | 2 GiB |
| Start to first healthy response | 60 s |
| Concurrent requests | up to 50 in flight |
| Per-request timeout | 5 s (10 s for `POST /_test/reset`) |
| Outbound network | available during `docker build`, **none at run time** |
| Disk | ephemeral; state need not survive a container restart |

Runtime assets and dependencies must be included in the image. This includes fonts,
scripts and stylesheets; external services are unavailable at runtime.

## 3. Runtime contract

### 3.1 Listening

Listen on `0.0.0.0` using the `PORT` environment variable, default `8080`.

### 3.2 Health

```http
GET /health  ->  200  {"status": "ok"}
```

Return 200 once the service and its data store can serve requests, within 60 seconds
of container start. Non-200 responses are permitted before the service is ready.

### 3.3 Reset and seed

```http
POST /_test/reset
Content-Type: application/json

{ ...fixture... }

->  204 No Content
```

Replace all service state with the fixture in the request body (§4). When reset returns
204, subsequent requests must see only that fixture. Repeated resets are supported.
This test endpoint must be enabled in the delivered image and requires no authentication.

### 3.4 Conventions

- Requests and responses are `application/json; charset=utf-8`.
- Timestamps in responses are RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, e.g. `2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00`.
- Unknown fields in a request body are ignored, never an error.
- Unknown query parameters are ignored.
- IDs are opaque strings of at most 64 characters. Their format is yours. This limit
  also applies to IDs supplied in reset fixtures.

## 4. Model

Restaurants and tables are supplied through `POST /_test/reset` only. Restaurant and
table creation endpoints are out of scope.

| Field | On | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `timezone` | Restaurant | IANA zone name, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. All of the restaurant's times are local to this |
| `slot_minutes` | Restaurant | Bookings start on a grid of this many minutes from opening time |
| `reservation_duration_minutes` | Restaurant | How long every reservation occupies its table |
| `cancellation_cutoff_minutes` | Restaurant | A booking cannot be cancelled or changed within this many minutes of its start |
| `opening_hours` | Restaurant | Per weekday. A day with no entry is closed |
| `capacity` | Table | Maximum party size |

### Fixture format

```json
{
  "users": [
    { "id": "u_ada", "email": "ada@example.com",
      "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada" }
  ],
  "restaurants": [
    {
      "id": "r_anker",
      "name": "Zum Anker",
      "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
      "slot_minutes": 30,
      "reservation_duration_minutes": 90,
      "cancellation_cutoff_minutes": 120,
      "opening_hours": [
        { "weekday": "thu", "opens": "18:00", "closes": "23:00" },
        { "weekday": "fri", "opens": "18:00", "closes": "23:30" }
      ],
      "tables": [
        { "id": "t_1", "label": "1", "capacity": 2 },
        { "id": "t_2", "label": "2", "capacity": 4 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "reservations": []
}
```

- `weekday` is one of `mon tue wed thu fri sat sun`.
- `opens` and `closes` are local `HH:MM`, 24-hour. `closes` is always later than `opens` on the
  same local day — opening hours never cross midnight.
- Seeded users must be able to log in with the given password immediately.
- `reservations` may seed confirmed bookings, with the same fields as a `POST /reservations`
  body plus `id`, `reference` and `user_id`.

Fixtures may use any calendar date. A booking must not be rejected solely because its
start is in the past; the cancellation and amendment cutoff rules still apply.

## 5. Errors

Every 4xx and 5xx response carries this body:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "table_unavailable", "message": "human readable, any wording" } }
```

Use the specified HTTP status and `code`. The human-readable `message` may use any wording.
Endpoint-specific errors are listed with each endpoint.

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `malformed_request` | Unparseable body, or a field of the wrong JSON type |
| 400 | `missing_idempotency_key` | Required `Idempotency-Key` header absent or empty |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token |
| 403 | `forbidden` | Authenticated, but not permitted to touch this resource |
| 404 | `not_found` | No such resource, or not visible to this caller |
| 409 | `idempotency_key_reuse` | Key already used by this caller with a different request body |
| 422 | `validation_failed` | A required field or query parameter is missing, or a stated rule is violated with no more specific code |

A field of the correct JSON type with an invalid format or out-of-range value gives
422 `validation_failed`, unless an endpoint specifies a different error. This includes
invalid dates, negative counts and values exceeding a stated maximum or length. In addition:

- Endpoint-specific field rules take precedence: invalid `party_size` values (including strings
  and booleans) and `starts_at_local` strings that are not a bare local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` are
  422 `validation_failed`. Other wrong JSON types follow the rule below.
- An integer-valued **query parameter** is written as plain decimal digits: `1e9`, `4.0` and `+4`
  are 422 `validation_failed` whatever their numeric value.
- Reserve 400 `malformed_request` for a body that does not parse or a field of the wrong type.

Shared ranges, enforced on every endpoint that takes them:

| Field | Valid | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | 1 to 255 characters | 422 `validation_failed` |

Requests must not produce 5xx responses, including under concurrent load.

## 6. Authentication

Authentication supports signup and login. Email verification, password reset, refresh
tokens and role-management endpoints are out of scope. Permissions specified elsewhere
in these requirements still apply.

```http
POST /auth/signup
{ "email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada" }

->  201  { "user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..." }
```

```http
POST /auth/login
{ "email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse" }

->  200  { "user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..." }
```

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Email already registered | 409 `email_taken` |
| Password shorter than 8 characters | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `email` not of the form `local@domain` | 422 `validation_failed` |
| Wrong password or unknown email on login | 401 `unauthenticated` |

Every other endpoint requires a bearer token, except `/health`, `/_test/reset`, the two above, and
the three public endpoints named at the top of §8 — `GET /restaurants`, `GET /restaurants/{id}` and
`GET /availability`:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Tokens do not expire. An account may have multiple valid tokens and concurrent sessions.

Passwords must be stored using a password-hashing function such as bcrypt, scrypt or
Argon2, or an equivalent. Plaintext password storage is not permitted.

## 7. Idempotency

Two write paths require an idempotency key: **`POST /reservations`** (§8) and
**`POST /reservation-moves`** (§11).

```http
Idempotency-Key: <client-chosen string, 1..255 characters>
```

The key is scoped to **the authenticated user**. Two different users may use the same key string
with no interaction between them.

A replay means the same user sending the **same method, the same path and the same body**. The
same key with the same body on a different path is a different request, not a replay, and must
succeed normally.

After the body has been parsed as a JSON object and the caller authenticated, idempotency
is resolved before endpoint-specific field validation or current-resource checks. Thus a
used key with a different JSON body returns `409 idempotency_key_reuse` even when that new
body would otherwise be invalid.

| Situation | Response |
|---|---|
| Header absent or empty | 400 `missing_idempotency_key` |
| First use of the key | The normal response, **201** |
| Replay: same key, same body | **200**, body identical to the original response as a JSON value |
| Same key, different body | 409 `idempotency_key_reuse` |
| Key reused after the original request failed with 4xx | Treated as a first use |

"Same body" means the same JSON value after parsing — key order and whitespace do not matter.

For concurrent identical requests with an unused key, exactly one returns 201.
The others return 200 with the same body. The operation takes effect only once.

A successful replay returns the original response, even after the resource changes or
is cancelled. It makes no further state changes.

## 8. API

`GET /restaurants`, `GET /restaurants/{id}` and `GET /availability` are **public** — no bearer
token. Everything else needs one. Diners browse before they sign in.

### `GET /restaurants`

```json
{ "restaurants": [ { "id": "r_anker", "name": "Zum Anker", "timezone": "Europe/Berlin" } ] }
```

### `GET /restaurants/{id}`

The restaurant with its `slot_minutes`, `reservation_duration_minutes`,
`cancellation_cutoff_minutes`, `opening_hours` and `tables`, in the fixture's shape. 404 if
unknown.

### `GET /availability`

```http
GET /availability?restaurant_id=r_anker&date=2026-09-24&party_size=4
```

All three parameters are required; a missing one is 422 `validation_failed`. `date` is a local
calendar date at the restaurant.

```json
{
  "restaurant_id": "r_anker",
  "date": "2026-09-24",
  "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
  "slots": [
    { "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T18:00",
      "starts_at": "2026-09-24T18:00:00+02:00",
      "available_table_ids": ["t_2"] }
  ]
}
```

`starts_at_local` is the full `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` and goes into `POST /reservations` unchanged.

A slot appears for every `slot_minutes` step from `opens` such that
`slot + reservation_duration_minutes <= closes`. `available_table_ids` lists the tables of that
restaurant with `capacity >= party_size` and no overlapping confirmed reservation, in fixture
order. A slot with no available table still appears, with an empty list.

A closed day returns `"slots": []`.

### `POST /reservations`

`Idempotency-Key` is required; see §7.

```http
POST /reservations
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: 2f9c1a...

{ "restaurant_id": "r_anker", "table_id": "t_2",
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00", "party_size": 4 }
```

`starts_at_local` is wall-clock at the restaurant, with no offset and no `Z`. Resolve it against
the restaurant's `timezone`.

```json
201
{
  "reservation_id": "res_7",
  "reference": "K3P7QW",
  "restaurant_id": "r_anker",
  "table_id": "t_2",
  "party_size": 4,
  "status": "confirmed",
  "starts_at_local": "2026-09-24T19:00",
  "starts_at": "2026-09-24T19:00:00+02:00",
  "ends_at": "2026-09-24T20:30:00+02:00",
  "created_at": "2026-09-21T11:04:03+00:00"
}
```

`reference` is 6 to 12 characters of `A-Z0-9`, unique across all reservations, and never changes.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| The table is taken for an overlapping interval | 409 `table_unavailable` |
| `starts_at_local` is not on the slot grid | 422 `not_on_slot_grid` |
| Slot outside opening hours, or the reservation would end after `closes` | 422 `outside_opening_hours` |
| `party_size` exceeds the table's `capacity` | 422 `party_exceeds_capacity` |
| `party_size` below 1, or not an integer | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `starts_at_local` is a local time that does not exist (see §9) | 422 `invalid_local_time` |
| Unknown restaurant, unknown table, or the table belongs to another restaurant | 404 `not_found` |

### `GET /reservations`

The caller's reservations, `starts_at` descending, confirmed and cancelled alike.
Return `200` with `{"reservations": [...]}`; each entry has the same shape as the
create response. An empty list is `{"reservations": []}`.

### `GET /reservations/{reference}`

One reservation. **404 if it is not the caller's** — do not leak the existence of other people's
bookings.

### `POST /reservations/{reference}/cancel`

```json
200
{ "reference": "K3P7QW", "status": "cancelled", ... }
```

Frees the table immediately: the next `GET /availability` must offer that slot again.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Already cancelled | 200 with the current state — cancelling twice is not an error |
| Now is within `cancellation_cutoff_minutes` of `starts_at`, or later | 409 `cutoff_passed` |
| Not the caller's reservation | 404 `not_found` |

### `PATCH /reservations/{reference}`

Change the time, the table or the party size. Any subset of `table_id`, `starts_at_local`,
`party_size`. No idempotency key is required here.

Validation is identical to `POST /reservations`, and the same cutoff rule as cancel applies
(409 `cutoff_passed`), measured against the **current** start time. A cancelled reservation is
409 `reservation_cancelled`. A successful amendment releases the old slot and reserves the
new one together. A failed amendment leaves the original booking and its occupancy unchanged.

`reference` and `reservation_id` survive a change.

## 9. Time and DST

Local dates and times follow the restaurant's `timezone`, including daylight-saving transitions.

**Spring forward.** Local times in the skipped hour do not exist. They never appear in
availability, and booking one is 422 `invalid_local_time`.

**Fall back.** Local times in the repeated hour occur twice. **Always resolve to the first
occurrence — the one before the clocks change.** The slot appears once in availability, and the
second occurrence is not bookable.

`reservation_duration_minutes` is **absolute time**, not wall-clock. A 90-minute reservation
starting at 01:30 on a fall-back night ends 90 real minutes later, and its local `ends_at` will
read 02:00, not 03:00.

The transitions that must be handled:

| Zone | Spring forward | Fall back |
|---|---|---|
| `Europe/Berlin` | 2026-03-29, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-10-25, 03:00 → 02:00 |
| `America/New_York` | 2026-03-08, 02:00 → 03:00 | 2026-11-01, 02:00 → 01:00 |

Offsets must follow the IANA rules for the specified zone and date.

## 10. Export and import

The service must support `GET /_test/export` and `POST /_test/import`. Like reset, these
are unauthenticated test endpoints.
Exports may contain credentials and session tokens; handle them as private test artifacts.
Return 200 from export with a JSON object containing `track: "tablekeeper"`,
`format_version: 1` and `state` (an implementation-defined JSON object). The state format
is opaque to the caller and must be accepted unchanged by import.

Import takes that entire object and atomically replaces the service's state, returning
204. It must accept an unchanged export produced by this service. No dependency on the
source process, files, volume, port or network address is allowed. Import is replacement,
not merge; repeating it restores the exported state without duplicating anything. Invalid
JSON follows §5; missing fields, wrong track/version or an invalid state give 422
`validation_failed` without changing the destination. Test control calls have a 10-second
timeout. Export is an atomic, read-only snapshot; subsequent source writes do not change it.

Preserve accounts and hashed-password login, existing bearer tokens, fixture configuration,
reservations, references, all completed idempotent request bodies and original responses.
Identities, statuses and timestamps must not be regenerated. Failed request keys remain
reusable. Existing receipts, references, tokens and retries must remain valid after import;
replacing the state with a fresh fixture does not satisfy this requirement. Import removes
all previous destination data and credentials. Reset continues to clear all state, including
imported state. State need not survive an abrupt container restart.

## 11. Atomic reservation moves

A diner may change several bookings in one request.

`POST /reservation-moves` requires authentication and an idempotency key. Body:

```json
{"moves": [{"reference": "BOOK01", "table_id": "t_2"},
           {"reference": "BOOK02", "table_id": "t_1"}]}
```

`moves` contains 1..8 objects with distinct string references. Invalid shape or duplicate
references gives 422 `validation_failed`. Every booking must belong to the caller and the
same restaurant. Unknown/another owner's reference gives 404 `not_found`; different
restaurants give 422 `validation_failed`. No token gives 401.

Each item accepts the ordinary PATCH fields `table_id`, `starts_at_local`, `party_size`;
omitted fields retain their current values and unknown fields are ignored. The booking's
identity, owner and creation time never change. Cancelled bookings give 409
`reservation_cancelled`. Each booking's existing cutoff applies. Non-occupancy errors use
ordinary amendment codes and take precedence in input order, with cutoff errors preceding
other changes for that booking. An overlap among resulting bookings or with an unlisted
booking gives 409 `table_unavailable`. Unchanged listed bookings retain their occupancy.

Either every move commits or nothing changes: occupancy, reservation records and retry
keys. On success return 201 with `{"reservations": [...]}` in input order, including
unchanged items.
Replays return that original response with 200, even after amendments or cancellations.
No-op moves retain all existing values. Export/import preserves successful batch receipts
as well as the resulting bookings. No batch UI is required.
===== END OF REQUIREMENTS =====

# Tablekeeper — stage 1

An HTTP reservations service. Everything it needs is in the image: the store is
in memory and the IANA timezone database is compiled into the binary, so the
container needs no outbound network, no volume and no companion service.

## Build and run

```sh
docker build -t tablekeeper stage-1
docker run --rm -e PORT=8080 -p 8080:8080 tablekeeper
```

Then:

```sh
curl -s localhost:8080/health
# {"status":"ok"}
```

`PORT` selects the listening port and defaults to `8080`; the service always
listens on `0.0.0.0`. The container answers `GET /health` with
`200 {"status": "ok"}` within a second of starting.

State is in memory and ephemeral: it does not survive a container restart, which
is what the requirements call for. Seed it with `POST /_test/reset`, move it with
`GET /_test/export` and `POST /_test/import`.

```sh
curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/_test/reset -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     --data @fixture.json -i | head -1
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```

I rejected Tablekeeper stage 1 at commit `126cf6bc` and sent the verdict to the coordinator with commands, output and reproductions for each finding.

The image builds cleanly, starts and runs with no outbound network, and the 120 supplied partial checks pass. My own probes, written from the spec, found three defects:

1. **Invalid import wipes the service (blocking).** Importing `{"track":"tablekeeper","format_version":1,"state":{}}`, or a state with only unknown keys, returns 204 and erases all existing data. The spec says an invalid state must return 422 and change nothing.
2. **Daylight-saving closing-time check is wrong (blocking).** The check of a booking's end against closing time adds the duration as wall-clock minutes. The spec says the duration is real elapsed time. It fails both ways:
   - Berlin, 29 March 2026, closing 03:30: a 01:30 booking is accepted even though its own `ends_at` reads 04:00.
   - New York, 1 November 2026, closing 02:30: the spec's own 01:30 example is rejected, although it really ends at 02:00. Availability has the same error.
3. **Wrong error for an unknown token.** On the two write endpoints, an unknown token without an `Idempotency-Key` gets 400. With an over-long key it gets 422. It should get 401, which is what a missing token already gets.

I also tested the coder's nine declared choices against the spec. Choices 1 (extra body fields count for idempotency) and 7 (reset/import reject inconsistent fixtures) hold up. One claim is false: a badly formatted `starts_at_local` is checked after the restaurant lookup, not before. The spec doesn't fix that order, so I didn't reject on it.

Everything else I tested behaved as the spec requires: error codes, idempotency, concurrency, the other daylight-saving cases, cancel and amend, batch moves, export/import, password hashing and the time limits.

I tested my own copy, made with `git archive` of that commit, not the working tree. I ran `docker build --no-cache` and started it with `--cpus 2 --memory 2g -e PORT=...`.
- **Clean build and run:** OK. `/health` returned 200 about 150 ms after start.
- **No network at run time:** OK. On a `docker network create --internal` network, `/health` returned 200 from a peer container, and outbound to example.com was blocked.
- **Supplied partial checks** (`kickoff/tablekeeper/test/stage_1`, run unedited): 120 passed.
- **My own probes:** about 300 assertions written from the spec. Two blocking defects and one precedence defect, below.

== BLOCKING ==

**F1. Import accepts an invalid state and wipes the destination (§10).**
§10 says an invalid state must give 422 validation_failed without changing the destination.
- I seeded the destination with a user, a token and a restaurant.
- I ran `POST /_test/import {"track":"tablekeeper","format_version":1,"state":{}}`.
- Result: 204. Afterwards `GET /restaurants` returned `{"restaurants":[]}` and the old token got 401. The destination was wiped.
- `"state":{"bogus":1}` behaves the same: 204 and wiped.
- Every export this service produces contains users, tokens, restaurants, reservations and receipts. A state missing all of them is not something it can produce, so it is invalid.
- What is rejected correctly: wrong track, version 2, version "1", missing state, missing track, state as a string or null, users of the wrong type, a reservation with a bad reference. All gave 422 with the destination unchanged. Malformed JSON gave 400.
- Cause: `testctl.go` handleImport unmarshals into `state`, and `prepare()` accepts nil slices and maps.

**F2. Across a DST change, the closing-time check uses wall-clock minutes instead of real time (§8 with §9).**
§9 says the duration is absolute time. §8 says a booking that would end after `closes` is 422 outside_opening_hours. Both `resolveAgainstHours` and `slotsOn` instead check `stamp.minutes + DurationMinutes <= closes`. It fails in both directions:
- **(a) Accepts a booking that ends after close.** Europe/Berlin on 2026-03-29, open sun 00:00–03:30, 90 minutes. POST 01:30 gives 201 with `"ends_at":"2026-03-29T04:00:00+02:00"`. The service's own ends_at is after closes 03:30. 01:30 also appears in availability.
- **(b) Rejects a booking that ends before close.** America/New_York on 2026-11-01, open sun 00:00–02:30. POST 01:30 gives 422 outside_opening_hours, and availability stops at 01:00. This is the spec's own example: 01:30 plus 90 real minutes ends at 02:00, which is before closes 02:30.
- Everything else in DST is correct; see "Verified OK" below.

**F3. An unknown token is not treated the same as a missing token on idempotent writes (§5, §6, §7).**
§7 says the caller is authenticated before idempotency is resolved, and §5 says a missing, malformed or unknown token is 401.
- `POST /reservations` with no Authorization header gives 401.
- `Authorization: Bearer not-a-real-token` with no Idempotency-Key gives **400 missing_idempotency_key**.
- The same unknown token with a 300-character key gives **422 validation_failed**.
- `POST /reservation-moves` behaves the same way.
- Cause: `serveIdempotent` validates the key header before resolving the token under the lock. Unknown tokens should get 401 first.

== DECLARED CHOICES, CHECKED AGAINST THE TEXT ==
1. **Unknown fields count toward the idempotency body:** consistent with §7, which defines "same body" as the same JSON value, and unknown fields are part of that value. Observed: same key plus an extra field gives 409. Accepted.
2. **party_size 4.0 gives 422:** defensible under §8 ("not an integer"), and the spec does not decide it. Accepted.
3. **display_name required on signup:** the spec does not require it. Side effect: signup with an already-taken email and no display_name gives 422, not the 409 email_taken from §6. Risk only, not a rejection ground.
4. **Precedence:** the claim does not hold for `starts_at_local`. Its format is checked after the restaurant/table lookup: unknown restaurant plus `starts_at_local:"garbage"` gives 404. The spec is silent on this order, so it is not a rejection ground, but either the claim or the code should be corrected. The booking-rule order (invalid_local_time, then grid, then hours, then capacity, then table_unavailable; closed day gives outside_opening_hours) matches the claim.
5. **Batch order:** matches §11 as implemented per booking. Item 1's 422 wins over item 2's cutoff. For the same booking, cutoff wins over its other changes. Ownership 404 and the different-restaurants 422 are checked across the whole batch first.
6. **Unchanged fields not revalidated:** fine.
7. **Reset/import reject inconsistent fixtures:** the spec defines no reset failure, so the only risk is rejecting a fixture the harness sends.
   - Accepted: seeded `status:"cancelled"`; seeds without id or reference; a restaurant without opening_hours; closes 24:00; an off-grid seed.
   - Rejected with 422: a seed `created_at` ending in "Z" (valid RFC 3339; the parser only takes numeric offsets), a lowercase reference, an id over 64 characters.
   - Low risk, since §4 seeds don't list created_at. Note that a fixture with a Z created_at would fail the whole reset.
8. **IDs over 64 characters give 422:** consistent with §3.4 and §5.
9. **Unknown method gives 404 with the error envelope:** acceptable, since §5 has no 405 code.

== VERIFIED OK (observed myself) ==
- **Signup and login:** 201/200 with the right shape; 409 email_taken; 422 for passwords under 8 characters and for bad emails; 401 for a wrong password or unknown email; multiple tokens per account all valid.
- **401 on reads:** missing, malformed, Basic and unknown tokens all get 401.
- **Password storage:** stored as bcrypt `$2a$08$`; no plaintext in the export.
- **§5 error codes and types:** malformed or array body 400; wrong-type id fields 400; party_size "2", true, 0, -1, 2.5 or null all 422; bad starts_at_local (Z, offset, seconds, space, Feb 30, 25:00, empty) all 422; a missing required field 422; missing or empty key 400; a 256-character key 422 while 255 is OK.
- **Availability query:** 4.0, +4, 1e9, -1, 0, abc and empty all 422; a missing parameter 422; a bad date 422; an unknown restaurant 404; unknown parameters ignored.
- **Booking rules:**
  - Overlap gives 409; a booking at 20:30 after a 90-minute 19:00 booking is free.
  - Off-grid gives 422 not_on_slot_grid; before opening or ending after close gives 422 outside_opening_hours.
  - Party over capacity gives 422; an unknown restaurant, an unknown table, or another restaurant's table gives 404.
  - A booking in the past is not rejected for that alone.
  - Unknown body fields are ignored.
- **Idempotency:**
  - Reordered or reformatted body replays 200 with an identical body; different body 409, even when the new body is invalid.
  - Another user's identical key is independent. The same key on another path is not a replay.
  - A key that failed with 4xx is reusable. A replay after cancel returns the original confirmed body and does not re-occupy the table.
  - 25 concurrent identical requests, 3 trials: exactly one 201 and 24 × 200, all identical bodies, one effect each.
- **Concurrency** (Go load generator inside the Docker network, 50 in flight, `--cpus 2`):
  - 50 logins all 200, slowest 2.48 s; 50 signups all 201, slowest 2.0 s.
  - Five rounds of 50 bookings fighting for one table/slot: one 201 per round, the rest 409, all under 54 ms.
  - Mixed load of 5000 requests (book, availability, list, patch, cancel, moves): codes only 200/201/409, slowest 76 ms, 0 overlapping confirmed pairs in the export.
  - 40 conflicting concurrent moves: one booking wins the target.
- **Cancel and PATCH:**
  - Cancel frees the slot; cancelling twice gives 200; 404 for someone else's or an unknown booking.
  - Cutoff gives 409 for cancel and for PATCH, including PATCH to a distant time (measured against the current start), and for a booking that has already started.
  - PATCH keeps reference and reservation_id; it can overlap its own old interval; failed PATCHes (409, 422, 404, 400) leave the booking and occupancy unchanged; a cancelled booking gives 409 reservation_cancelled.
  - The list is sorted by starts_at descending, including cancelled bookings; other users' bookings are hidden (404).
- **DST:**
  - Berlin and New York spring-forward hours are missing from availability, and booking them gives 422 invalid_local_time.
  - Fall-back repeated slots appear once with the earlier offset (+02:00 / -04:00).
  - NY 01:30 ends 02:00-05:00, Berlin 02:30 ends 03:00+01:00, and occupancy is measured in real time. Summer and winter offsets are correct.
- **Moves:**
  - A swap gives 201 in input order; a replay gives 200 with the same body, even after later amendments; key reuse gives 409, including with an invalid body.
  - Twelve failure cases each returned the expected code and left `GET /reservations` byte-identical: 3rd item over capacity, 2nd off-grid, overlap with an unlisted booking, overlap within the batch, duplicate references, 0 or 9 moves, missing or non-object moves, unknown reference, someone else's booking, unknown table.
  - Also: a cancelled booking gives 409; different restaurants give 422; no token 401; no key 400; a failed key is reusable; no-op moves keep their values.
- **Export/import** (two separate containers):
  - Export envelope is correct; the snapshot is unchanged by later source writes.
  - Import removes the destination's own users, tokens and restaurants. Afterwards, old tokens and signup tokens work, and bcrypt logins work.
  - Reservations are identical: ids, references, statuses and timestamps.
  - Create and move receipts replay 200 with identical bodies; key reuse gives 409; a failed key is reusable.
  - Occupancy is correct, and new references are unique.
  - Importing twice re-exports exactly the original, with no duplicates. Reset clears imported state.
- **Time limits:** reset with 200 bcrypt users and 1500 seeded bookings took 2.4–6.1 s; export and import of that state took under 1 s; 200 availability requests at 50 concurrent finished in under 5 s.

== NOT ESTABLISHED / RISKS ==
- Reset time grows with the number of seeded users, because each password is hashed (6.1 s at 200 users on 2 CPUs). A fixture of roughly 300 or more users could exceed the 10 s limit.
- I did not test a 60 s start under load, a container restart, or request bodies over 8 MB.
- A whitespace-only Idempotency-Key is treated as missing (400); the spec only says "absent or empty".
- From code review only: login checks the password outside the lock, then looks the user up again by ID. A reset in between could issue a token for a different account with the same ID. I did not reproduce this.

To fix: F1 (import must require the state's members and reject anything this service couldn't have exported); F2 (compare the real local end time against closes, in both booking and availability); F3 (resolve the bearer token before validating the Idempotency-Key header). Reconcile choice 4 with the code. I'll re-verify on a new revision.
